explanation: The server validates the prompt and experiment controls before entering runAgent. Those controls configure real SDK behaviour.
The reset restores every demo input from immutable fixtures before a run. This reproduces the buggy auth task and its unchanged tests.
One query receives the selected task and scenario-specific options. The inspect scenario uses a read-only task; all subsequent interactions remain inside this one SDK conversation.
The observer identifies system initialization and optional partial events. Each is counted as a message without automatically becoming another model turn.
These actual options configure the SDK model request and choose available tools for read-only or repair mode. The SDK performs model API transport internally.
The tool_use branch records actual request IDs and associates them with an observed response group. The model, rather than the dashboard, decides which requests arrive.
The PreToolUse hook checks the application guard, reports denied calls, or records a permitted call start. Tool execution itself is implemented by the SDK.
The user-message branch observes returned tool feedback and its error status. Actual execution output is handled by the SDK; this app projects its identifiers and summary.
tool_result.tool_use_id finds the earlier request and response group. This actual join explains which call produced the feedback.
The same query iterator is consumed while the SDK feeds tool results back to the model and repeats internally. There is no extra application-level call that fabricates this feedback.
The typed result is projected without relabelling a limit as success. Its actual stop reason and token counts are preserved alongside the session, turns and estimated cost.
The finally block closes the conversation, reads the real auth file and emits independent checks. This still happens after a deliberate limit or read-only run.
The workspace handler highlights the actual source and renders each independent check. Verified repair requires changed source and all checks passing; read-only and stopped outcomes stay distinct.
